LESSON: AUDITORY DISCRIMINATION

Grade: PP1
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: LISTENING
Topic 1.5: Auditory discrimination

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Auditory discrimination
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: What sounds do different environment. whistles, phone ringing, hooting animals produce?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. Respond appropriately to among others. 3. Which sounds in the school sounds in the environment. • Learners could be guided to go environment call for specific

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Auditory discrimination

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Auditory discrimination

Teach
• Focus skill: Respond appropriately to among others. 3. Which sounds in the school sounds in the environment. • Learners could be guided to go environment call for specific.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Auditory discrimination.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Auditory discrimination
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What sounds do different environment. whistles, phone ringing, hooting animals produce?
2. where they identify 4. How are children expected to sounds they hear. respond to such sounds?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
